newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - July 29.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Tuesday's Daily Variety:
* The CBS-TV network posted a $7 million loss in the second quarter, providing fresh evidence that ratings stability hasn't helped the network's profit picture.
* The British government has given a huge financial boost to Channel 4 by ending the minority web's obligation to pay more than $100 million a year to the rival ITV network.
* A throng of self-styled Internet film critics who invade studio test screenings and publish their reviews on the Web have studio marketing chiefs clicking their browsers in fury.

* New Line Cinema, re-establishing its indie powerhouse sensibility, Monday announced a $400 million revolving line of credit for production financing from a group of international banks led by ABN AMRO Bank N.V.
* Former Sony Corp of America president Michael Schulhof has re-emerged as chairman of Animation Science Corp., a Sunnyvale, Calif.-based animation software firm.
* Columbia Pictures will make a movie based on "Spite House: The Last Secret of the Vietnam War," a non-fiction book by Monica Jensen-Stevenson.

* To "reduce the hype factor," the Academy of Motion Picture Arts & Sciences has revised its rules on Oscar promotions, banning review quotes and phone solicitations, and offering stricter definition about the distribution of music and screenplays to its members for award consideration.
